rows.subtype: Stage 1: A hurt that is not spoken [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager feels ignored when her friend sits with others at lunch. She is too proud to ask about it and too hurt to act normal, so she says nothing and turns her face away.
graph_context: next stage: Withholding as protection
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: pride, hurt

rows.description: Not replying feels safer than risking a fight or hearing "you are overreacting". Silence gives her a sense of control, and part of her hopes the friend will notice and come to her.
graph_context: previous stage: A hurt that is not spoken
next stage: Confusion for the one ignored
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: hope, trust

rows.subtype: Stage 3: Confusion for the one ignored [Receiver]
rows.description: The friend cannot tell what she did. Being unanswered feels like exclusion, so she guesses wildly, rereads old chats and grows anxious, which is precisely why silence hurts more than open anger.
graph_context: previous stage: Withholding as protection
next stage: Silence hardens into punishment
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: anger, anxiety, confusion, hurt

rows.description: Days pass and the silence becomes a message: you should know what you did. The teen enjoys being wanted back yet feels lonelier, and with every day, breaking the silence gets more embarrassing.
graph_context: previous stage: Confusion for the one ignored
next stage: Naming the pattern kindly
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: embarrassment, loneliness

rows.description: The friend sends "I can feel you are upset and I do not know why. I would rather hear it, even if it is bad." An invitation without accusation makes speaking safer than staying quiet.
graph_context: previous stage: Silence hardens into punishment
next stage: Speaking the real hurt
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: trust

rows.description: The teen says "I felt left out at lunch." The reply is usually smaller than the fear, and both learn that saying it early costs less than months of quiet distance.
graph_context: previous stage: Naming the pattern kindly
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: fear, hurt

rows.description: After a harsh argument a spouse feels flooded and goes silent, unable to find words that would not make things worse. He may not intend punishment at first; he simply has no way to cope with the intensity.
graph_context: next stage: Stonewalling becomes a habit
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: detachment, overwhelm

rows.description: Silence works in the short term, ending the shouting. Over time it becomes his automatic answer to conflict, and the unresolved issues pile up behind a wall of politeness.
graph_context: previous stage: Withdrawal after conflict
next stage: The partner's escalating alarm
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: determination

rows.description: She feels invisible and powerless, tries everything from questions to tears, then goes cold herself. Being shut out touches old fears of not mattering, and hurt often turns into anger.
graph_context: previous stage: Stonewalling becomes a habit
next stage: Mutual freeze
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: anger, fear, hurt

rows.description: Both now avoid the subject, the house is quiet, and each is waiting for the other to move. Pride and fear of another bad fight keep them stuck while the distance quietly grows.
graph_context: previous stage: The partner's escalating alarm
next stage: The breaking of the ice
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: fear, pride
